name: Shimla
tagline: Colonial hill-station grandeur amid Himalayan cedar forests.
whenBlurb: Spring and early summer are pleasant and green; late December brings snow and the Winter Carnival. Avoid the July-to-September monsoon and its landslides.

ourTake.lede: Shimla is at its best out of season and out of the town centre; the Mall Road crush is precisely what to avoid, so base yourself a little outside and use the town for its colonial architecture and walks. The toy-train up from Kalka is a genuine pleasure and worth building the trip around. Come in spring or autumn; peak summer and the snow-season weekends bring Delhi's traffic with them.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a colonial hill station, the toy train and cool pine air near Delhi.
ourTake.skipIf: You want to dodge peak-season crowds, or want a beach.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Wildflower Hall, An Oberoi Resort, Shimla
credentials: The Oberoi Group, flagship Himalayan resort
Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Travel Awards, ranked among Asia's best resorts
Travel + Leisure India, recognised luxury resort
Former residence of Lord Kitchener, Commander-in-Chief of the British Army in India
items.description: The former estate of Lord Kitchener, reborn as a cedar-forest Oberoi palace, the Himalayan icon of Indian luxury.

items.name: The Oberoi Cecil, Shimla
credentials: The Oberoi Group, heritage flagship in the city
Established 1884; the founding Oberoi property, reopened 1997 after full restoration
Ministry of Tourism, Heritage classification
items.description: Shimla's most storied address since 1884, the hotel where Mohan Singh Oberoi began, restored to hushed colonial grandeur.

items.name: The Oberoi Clarkes, Shimla
credentials: The Oberoi Group, heritage property
Built 1898; one of Shimla's oldest hotels and the first owned by the Oberoi group
Ministry of Tourism, upgraded to Heritage Grand classification (2012)
items.description: A grand colonial bungalow on the Mall since 1898, the first hotel the Oberoi group ever owned, intimate and full of history.

items.name: The Chalets Naldehra
credentials: Set on the Naldehra golf estate, the golf course laid out in 1905 by Lord Curzon, among the oldest in Asia
Boutique alpine-chalet resort, ~19 rooms and cottages
items.description: A boutique estate of chalets at 7,000 feet, wrapped around Asia's oldest golf course among the deodars.

items.name: Koti Resort, Shimla, Radisson Individuals Retreats
credentials: Radisson Individuals Retreats, member property
Hilltop resort in the Mashobra hills near Shimla
items.description: A hilltop retreat in the Mashobra forest with colonial warmth, Himalayan views and Radisson-backed service.

items.name: The Koti Village Resort, Kufri
credentials: Hilltop resort at ~2,400m near Kufri
Luxury cottages with panoramic Himalayan and Shimla-city views
items.description: Luxe glamping-style cottages at 8,000 feet, with 180-degree Himalayan panoramas above Kufri.

items.name: The Ridge
items.description: The great open promenade at 2,200 metres where all of Shimla gathers, the snow peaks lined up beyond Christ Church and the timber gables. A gentle early-morning stroll here, before the day-trippers arrive, is the Queen of Hills at her most composed.

items.name: The Mall Road
items.description: The pedestrianised Raj-era spine of the town, its lamp-lit facades and colonnades running above the valley. A private guide turns the evening amble into a walk through Kipling's Simla; the antique jewellers and Kashmiri shawl merchants reward an unhurried browse.

items.name: Christ Church
items.description: The butter-yellow neo-Gothic church of 1844, one of the oldest in North India, its stained glass and clock tower the postcard image of Shimla. Step inside for the cool hush and the organ; the frescoes were designed by Rudyard Kipling's father, Lockwood.

items.name: The Gaiety Theatre
items.description: A jewel-box Victorian Gothic theatre of 1887 by Henry Irwin, restored to its plush red-and-gilt glory, where the Raj once staged its amateur dramatics. A guided visit lets you stand on the same boards trod by viceroys and, later, a young Prithviraj Kapoor.

items.name: Scandal Point
items.description: The open shoulder where the Mall meets the Ridge, named for the alleged elopement of a Patiala prince with a viceroy's daughter. The best free view in Shimla and the town's natural meeting place, framed against the peaks.

items.name: The Viceregal Lodge (Indian Institute of Advanced Study)
items.description: The vast Elizabethan-Jacobean stone palace of 1888 from which the British ruled India each summer, where the 1945 Simla Conference and the Partition talks unfolded. The guided tour of the panelled interiors and manicured lawns is the single grandest Raj experience in the hills.

items.name: Jakhoo Temple & the giant Hanuman
items.description: Shimla's highest point at 2,455 metres, crowned by a 108-foot saffron Hanuman visible from across the town, on the spot the Ramayana links to the god's rest. A serene, cedar-shaded pilgrimage above the bustle; watch your spectacles around the resident monkeys.

items.name: Jakhoo Ropeway
items.description: The glass-cabin aerial ropeway that lifts you from the Ridge to the Hanuman temple in minutes, sparing the steep forest climb and gifting a bird's-eye sweep of the ridgeline roofs. The dignified way up for elders and children in a multi-generation party.

items.name: Kalka–Shimla Toy Train
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Mountain Railways of India)
items.description: The narrow-gauge marvel of 1903 that climbs 96 km through 102 tunnels and over 800 bridges to the summer capital, best savoured in a chartered first-class or the glass-roofed dome car. A slow, cinematic ascent through the Shivaliks that no drive can rival.

items.name: Shimla State Museum
items.description: A colonial mansion on Mount Pleasant holding Pahari miniature paintings, Kangra bronzes, temple sculpture and Himachali textiles. A quiet, well-curated hour that gives the whole hill region its artistic context, away from the crowds.

items.name: Johnnie's Wax Museum
items.description: A small, playful wax gallery in the Willow Banks estate on the Mall, its London-made figures of film stars and cricketers a reliable hit with children. A light-hearted diversion to break up a heritage-heavy afternoon.

items.name: Kali Bari Temple
items.description: The 1845 Bengali temple to Goddess Shyamala, from whom Shimla takes its name, a five-minute walk off the Mall. A living shrine of quiet devotion and a fragrant, flower-strewn contrast to the promenade below.

items.name: Tara Devi Temple
items.description: A 250-year-old hilltop temple to the star goddess, brought from Bengal, ringed by deodar at 1,850 metres with long views back to Shimla. A peaceful, uncrowded stop on the road in, worth the short detour for the panorama alone.

items.name: Kamna Devi Temple, Prospect Hill
items.description: A short, pretty pine climb to a Kali shrine crowning Prospect Hill, rewarded with a 360-degree sweep over Shimla and the valleys. A gentle morning walk that locals prize far more than tourists do.

items.name: Annandale
items.description: A flat green saucer amid the hills, once the Raj's playground for polo, cricket and flower shows, now home to a golf course and the Army Heritage Museum. A rare piece of level ground in Shimla and a graceful, breezy afternoon.

items.name: Summer Hill
items.description: A leafy, quiet suburb where Mahatma Gandhi stayed at Georgian-style Rothney Castle's neighbourhood and where Himachal University now sits. A calm base for pine walks and a stop on the toy-train line, away from the Mall's crush.

items.name: Chadwick Falls
items.description: A 90-metre cascade plunging through deep deodar and oak forest, fullest and most dramatic just after the monsoon. A short trek through the Glen woods brings you to a cool, green amphitheatre far from the town noise.

items.name: The Glen Forest
items.description: A shaded stream-side hollow of dense pine below the Cecil, a favourite Raj-era picnic ground and gentle woodland ramble. Close enough to walk to, wild enough to feel a world away from the Mall.

items.name: Lakkar Bazaar
items.description: Shimla's old woodcraft market beside the Ridge, stacked with hand-carved walnut and deodar keepsakes, walking sticks and toys. The place to pick up an honest, made-in-the-hills souvenir rather than a factory trinket.

items.name: Green Valley
items.description: The photogenic saddle on the way to Kufri where the road opens onto rolling green slopes and, on clear days, distant snow. A classic pause for a chai and a photograph, deodars falling away on both sides.

items.name: Kufri
items.description: A high meadowed ridge at 2,720 metres with grandstand Himalayan views, pony rides up to Mahasu Peak and winter snow. Touristy at its heart but a soaring backdrop; go early, or ride above the crowds to the quieter tops.

items.name: Himalayan Nature Park, Kufri
items.description: A high-altitude wildlife park sheltering snow leopard, Himalayan black bear, musk deer and the state-bird Monal pheasant among the deodars. A gentle, shaded walk that turns Kufri into something the children will actually remember.

items.name: Naldehra Golf Course
items.description: A nine-hole (18-tee) course laid out by Lord Curzon in 1905 on a deodar-fringed ridge at 2,200 metres, so loved he named a daughter for it. Among the oldest and highest greens in India, and a rarefied morning even if you never lift a club.

items.name: Mashobra
items.description: A hushed forest village of apple orchards and cedar walks, home to the Presidential Retreat and to Shimla's most exclusive resort. The address to choose for quiet, orchard-scented seclusion within reach of the town.

items.name: Craignano
items.description: An Italianate villa and terraced garden on a knoll above Mashobra, built by an Italian craftsman in the 19th century, now a serene HPTDC nature spot. A little jewel of a picnic ground with wide valley views and almost no crowd.

items.name: Fagu
items.description: A tiny hamlet above Kufri wrapped in apple orchards and drifting mist, with long, uncluttered views over terraced valleys. A gentler, quieter alternative to Kufri for those who want the scenery without the ponies.

items.name: Chail Palace
items.description: The 1891 summer palace the Maharaja of Patiala built in pique after being barred from Shimla, set in cedar forest on its own hilltop. Stay or lunch amid the royal drawing rooms and lawns for a taste of princely, rather than viceregal, India.

items.name: Chail Cricket Ground
items.description: The world's highest cricket and polo ground at 2,444 metres, levelled from a hilltop in 1893 and now part of the Chail Military School. A remarkable, pine-ringed plateau in the sky, worth the drive for the sheer improbability of it.

items.name: Kali ka Tibba, Chail
items.description: A hilltop Kali temple crowning the ridge above Chail, reached through thick deodar and rewarded with a full-circle Himalayan panorama. The finest viewpoint in the Chail hills and blessedly uncommercial.

items.name: Chail Wildlife Sanctuary
items.description: A protected belt of pine, oak and deodar sheltering the Himalayan black bear, leopard, ghoral and cheer pheasant. A calm forest drive or guided birding walk for those who prefer nature to the tourist trail.

items.name: Tattapani Hot Springs
items.description: Sulphur-rich thermal springs on the banks of the Sutlej, long prized for easing aches and stiff joints, with riverside camps and riverbank massages. A restorative, off-beat day out that pairs a warm soak with dramatic gorge scenery.

items.name: Narkanda
items.description: A fir-forested town at 2,700 metres deep in the apple belt, a gateway to snow views and gentle winter skiing. The air turns crisp and the crowds thin here; it is Shimla's district as it was before the resorts arrived.

items.name: Hatu Peak
items.description: A 3,400-metre summit above Narkanda crowned by the old wooden Hatu Mata temple, with a huge sweep of snow ranges on a clear day. A short drive plus a walk to one of the most panoramic and least-visited tops near Shimla.

items.name: Kotgarh & Thanedar apple orchards
items.description: The cradle of Indian apple growing, where the American Satyanand Stokes planted the first commercial orchards in 1916, now heavy with blossom in spring and fruit in autumn. Stay in an orchard homestead and walk the terraces where the industry began.

items.name: Sangla Valley (Baspa Valley)
items.description: A green Kinnauri valley of apple and apricot orchards, timber-and-stone villages and the Baspa river, ringed by snow peaks. A farther, wilder day or two beyond Shimla, and the loveliest introduction to the Kinnaur hills.

items.name: Chitkul
items.description: The last inhabited village on the old Indo-Tibetan trade route, where the motorable road ends against the meadows and the roar of the young Baspa. Remote, elemental and unforgettable, best reached with a seasoned mountain driver.

items.name: Kalpa
items.description: An orchard village perched opposite the sacred 6,000-metre Kinner Kailash range, whose face turns gold at sunrise above the apple trees. A serene, high-altitude perch for those going deep into Kinnaur, rich in old wooden temples.

items.name: Kasauli
items.description: A tiny, unspoilt colonial hill town of cobbled lanes, timber cottages and Christ Church, cool and green year-round. A restful, low-key detour on the way up from the plains, entirely free of the Mall's bustle.

items.name: Barog
credentials: On the UNESCO Kalka–Shimla Railway line
items.description: A sleepy railway hamlet on the toy-train line, home to the line's longest tunnel and its famous ghost story, wrapped in pine. A quiet, storybook halt to alight at or lunch in on the slow ascent to Shimla.

items.name: Wildflower Hall, An Oberoi Resort
items.description: Once Lord Kitchener's forest retreat, now a grand cedar-clad Oberoi at 2,500 metres with an open-air spa whirlpool facing the snows. Shimla's most romantic address for a honeymoon or a multi-generation escape, run entirely on hydro power.

items.name: The Oberoi Cecil
items.description: The Mall's most storied hotel, a Heritage Grand where Raj society once danced in the ballroom, now all fireplaces, a soaring wood atrium and valley views. A stay that puts you inside old Simla itself, minutes from the Ridge.

items.name: Chapslee
items.description: The Kapurthala royal family's 1830s mansion, still lived-in and hosting guests among Gobelin tapestries, Murano chandeliers and Persian carpets, opened as one of India's first heritage hotels in 1976. Tea or a stay here is a private audience with the vanished aristocratic Simla.

items.name: Shaily Peak
items.description: A short pony ride or walk to a modest summit with sweeping views over apple slopes and, on a clear day, distant snow. An easy, rewarding leg-stretch for a family exploring the Kufri hills.

items.name: Kufri Fun World
items.description: A hilltop amusement park with a go-kart track and one of the world's highest rides, a burst of colour amid the deodars. An easy crowd-pleaser to keep children happy on a Kufri day.

items.name: The Restaurant at Wildflower Hall
items.area: Mashobra / Charabra (Wildflower Hall, An Oberoi Resort)
credentials: Inside Wildflower Hall, An Oberoi Resort, the region's defining hotel
The Oberoi Group signature dining
items.description: Indian, Asian and Continental cooking in a glass conservatory over the deodar forest, the grandest table in the Himalayas here.

items.name: Dining at The Oberoi Cecil
credentials: Inside The Oberoi Cecil, Shimla's founding heritage hotel
The Oberoi Group, heritage kitchen
items.description: All-day Indian and international cooking beneath the hotel's soaring wood-panelled atrium, heritage dining in the heart of Shimla.

items.name: Ashiana & Goofa
credentials: Run by Himachal Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation (HPTC)
Long-standing Ridge / Mall Road landmark, the twin Ashiana (upstairs) and Goofa (basement)
items.description: A Shimla institution run by Himachal Tourism, a landmark circular pavilion on the Ridge, with the cave-like Goofa below.

items.name: Baljees
credentials: Long-standing Mall Road institution, a multi-generational Shimla landmark
items.description: A Mall Road fixture for generations, the beloved bakery-restaurant famous for its sweets and unhurried Shimla mornings.

items.name: Wake & Bake Café
credentials: Long-standing Mall Road café, a Shimla favourite
items.description: The Mall's favourite all-day café, a balcony table over Shimla, from breakfast crêpes to late cake.

items.name: The Bar at Wildflower Hall
items.area: Mashobra / Charabra (Wildflower Hall, An Oberoi Resort)
credentials: Inside Wildflower Hall, An Oberoi Resort, the region's defining hotel
The Oberoi Group, signature Himalayan lounge and bar
items.description: A firelit lounge and bar in the old Kitchener estate, single malts and mountain quiet, the grandest nightcap in the hills.

items.name: The Big Dipper, Koti Resort
credentials: Inside Koti Resort, Shimla, Radisson Individuals Retreats
Fireside English-style bar with a craft-cocktail list
items.description: An English-style bar with a warm fireplace and craft cocktails, tucked into the Mashobra hills.

plan.heading: 3 days in Shimla, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Arrive at Wildflower Hall, Oberoi in Chharabra, Lord Kitchener's old estate high above Shimla, and take in the cedar forest and the snow line from the terrace.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A guided walk of the Ridge, Christ Church and the old Gaiety Theatre, then the Scandal Point and Mall in the cool of late afternoon.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Wildflower Hall's restaurant, with Himachali dishes among the classics and the deodars floodlit outside.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: The toy train and the Raj

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive down to board a heritage carriage on the Kalka–Shimla railway for a stretch of the UNESCO narrow-gauge line through its tunnels and curves.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Viceregal Lodge at Observatory Hill, seen properly with a historian, then the Himachal State Museum's miniatures.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A fireside dinner back at the hotel, with a Himalayan wine and the valley lights below.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A guided forest walk from Chharabra toward Kufri through the cedar and oak, with the high peaks opening up.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A private picnic lunch at a viewpoint over the Sutlej valley, then a spa afternoon at the Oberoi.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A quiet final dinner on the terrace before the descent to Kalka or Chandigarh.

items.name: Chharabra / Mashobra (above town)
items.description: Quiet forested ridges with the best heritage retreats; best for calm and views.

items.name: The Ridge / Mall (central Shimla)
items.description: The colonial heart with the church and promenade; convenient but crowded at peak times.

items.name: Chhota Shimla / Kasumpti
items.description: Residential and quieter, a short way from the centre; for a more local, less touristy base.

events.name: Summer Festival
events.note: A week of cultural performances and events on the Ridge, marking the start of the hill-station season.

events.name: Winter Carnival
events.note: A festive cold-season carnival with music and local culture as the snow sets in.

events.name: Sipi Fair
events.note: A traditional spring fair in nearby Mashobra, a window into local Pahari culture.

events.name: Peak snow season
events.note: The most reliable window for snowfall around Shimla and Kufri, though weekends draw heavy crowds.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: The old town centre is vehicle-free, so choose a hotel near the Ridge or Mall to avoid a steep uphill walk with luggage; evenings are cold at 2,200 metres, and the colonial-era Cecil or Wildflower Hall side offers the finest quiet above the crowds.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Chandigarh (IXC), then a three-to-four-hour chauffeured drive up to Shimla; the toy train from Kalka is a charming, unhurried alternative for part of the route.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car with driver to the edge of the town, then walking, as the Mall Road and the central ridge are pedestrian-only; hotels arrange porters and short transfers.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Jio and Airtel 4G is solid in town but drops on the surrounding hill roads; hotel wifi is the steadier option for work.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee; cards work along the Mall and at hotels, with cash useful for the bazaar and porters; tipping is modest.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: March to June brings pleasant 15-30C days, and December-January delivers snow; avoid July-September, when heavy monsoon and landslide-prone roads disrupt travel.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Shimla's own airstrip is limited, so fly to Chandigarh (IXC), then a scenic 3-3.5 hour drive up (about 115 km). Chandigarh takes direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru on IndiGo/Air India/Vistara; use the lounge at Delhi T3 or Mumbai before the short hop, and pre-book a car for the hill climb.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: Modest altitude of about 2,200m, no acclimatisation needed for most. No special vaccinations beyond routine cover. Safe hill town; the main caution is icy or landslide-prone roads in winter and monsoon. Drink sealed or filtered water.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Easy for vegetarians, with plentiful North Indian veg and Himachali dishes; Jain is understood at the heritage hotels if flagged. The Oberoi Cecil and Wildflower Hall do polished vegetarian menus, and the Mall Road cafes cover casual veg fare.
